name: Meeting Prep

inputs.name: Your role in the meeting (running it, supporting, interviewing)

steps.title: Refresh the company
steps.detail: Latest results, stock move, news flow, anything announced this week — the thing you’ll be embarrassed not to know.

steps.title: Profile the people
steps.detail: Backgrounds, tenure, past statements, what each attendee is likely to want from the meeting.

steps.title: Predict the agenda
steps.detail: What do THEY want to cover? Prepare for their meeting, not just yours.

steps.title: Prepare your questions
steps.detail: 3-5 questions that show preparation and move your objective forward.

steps.title: Anticipate theirs
steps.detail: What will they ask you? Draft crisp answers to the hard ones.

steps.title: Delegate 1
steps.detail: Compiling recent news, results and stock context

steps.title: Delegate 3
steps.detail: Drafting the one-page brief in standard format

sections.name: Meeting brief: company, people, agenda, questions
sections.detail: The 30-minute briefing routine: company snapshot, recent events, the counterparty’s likely agenda, who’s in the room and what they care about, plus the questions you should ask and the ones you’ll be asked.

outputs.sourcePolicy: Every figure cites the page or filing it was read from; nothing is stated without a source.

verification.description: News items are current and real — a fabricated "recent event" is fatal
People data matches the right person (name collisions are common)

humanCheckpoints: Your objective for the meeting and the one thing you must leave with
Which questions to actually ask given the room

display.jobToBeDone: Walk into any client, management or interview meeting knowing the company, the people and the agenda cold.
